值得閱讀的理由

  • 釐清名稱相似、用途卻截然不同的 Orchestrator 與 Swarm，避免選錯協作模式。
  • 了解各功能如何分配模型、工作與審查流程，並掌握不同方案的可用性及用量影響。
  • 透過實際範例比較 Swarm 與動態工作流程，幫助讀者依照任務規模與複雜度選擇工具。

摘要

Orchestrator：一位助手、兩種模型

作者指出，Orchestrator 並不是多位 AI 同時工作，而是由一位助手在對話中處理任務，並在背景搭配規劃模型與執行模型。規劃模型預設為 Gemini 4，負責理解需求、查看專案檔案並制定計畫；執行模型預設為 Gemini 4 Hydrogen，負責搜尋、修改檔案及執行測試。若執行遇到問題，或任務時間較長、使用者中途介入，規劃模型會再次檢視並協助調整。

適用對象與日常使用建議

Orchestrator 可透過輸入框下方的模型選單選用，也能在設定中的 Models 頁面調整新對話的預設模型組合。不過，它不開放給免費版或入門級 Google AI Plus，主要提供給 Google AI Pro、符合資格的 Google AI Ultra 裝置與企業方案。官方建議將它用於日常功能開發、修復錯誤及跨多個檔案整理；若任務需要極深度推理、存在資源競爭，或只是簡單編輯文件、撰寫小工具，則可改用推理能力更強的模型，或直接選擇快速模型。

Swarm：多位助手在共享看板協作

若要讓多位助手各自負責工作，可在輸入框輸入斜線並選擇 Swarm。原本的對話會成為協調者，負責拆分工作、建立任務說明與驗收標準，並在主對話回應使用者；實際執行則交由各自從新對話開始的工作者。通常每兩到四位工作者會配置一位審查者，負責檢查變更與執行測試，另有監督者在進度停滯時提醒團隊。所有提問、變更紀錄與測試結果都會公開在共享看板上；沒有任務的成員則會休眠，不消耗規劃配額。

Swarm 實例、用量與檔案衝突

作者以一個包含價格、名稱與日期的臨時專案示範：三個檔案各有一項錯誤，並需要為各自新增自動化測試。協調者將工作分派給三位工作者，再安排審查者進行最後查核；工作者回報修改內容與測試後，審查者執行全部 27 項測試，確認無誤後由協調者整理結果並回覆使用者。Swarm 在所有方案中皆可使用，但仍處於預覽階段，而且因每位工作者都是獨立代理，會消耗更多 Token。工作者共用專案檔案時可能發生衝突，因此可將任務按檔案切分，必要時也能讓各自使用獨立副本，完成後再合併。

Swarm 與動態工作流程的差異

斜線選單中的動態工作流程（runflow）適用於所有方案，內建執行環境，能透過簡短的 Python 腳本依序或同時啟動多位代理，也能儲存腳本以供重用。不過，這些代理看不到腳本內容，也無法查看彼此的工作，只能依照指定格式回傳結果。因此，若代理需要在執行途中彼此討論、整合工作，或透過看板檢視進度，應選 Swarm；若要對大量檔案重複執行相同的檢查、修改與複查步驟，則適合使用動態工作流程。

作者也簡要區分其他工具：Subagent 適合將研究、瀏覽或測試等小型獨立工作交給助手處理；Boost 適合多任務、資源衝突或複雜演算法等高難度問題；Teamwork 則可支援跨多階段的大型專案，例如完整遷移、系統模擬或深入研究，並以明確目標和分階段驗收推進。總結來說，Orchestrator 以一位代理搭配兩種模型，在節省用量與維持執行效率之間取得平衡；Swarm 則讓多位代理透過共享看板協作，適合能清楚拆分成獨立檔案或議題的工作。兩者沒有絕對優劣，應依任務需求選用，也不必為小改動動用整個團隊。

It's available in all plans, but the command prompt shows "preview and quota heavy," meaning it's still in preview and consumes a lot of tokens, as every worker is an independent agent. >> The dynamic workflow is the "runflow" option in the slash menu. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 透過作者與 AI 討論中島美雪歌曲的親身經驗，呈現 AI 如何用文字引發共鳴，也提醒讀者不要把動人的表達誤認為可靠的事實。
  • 提供實用的查證方法：遇到看似深刻的回答，可以追問依據，並分辨哪些是已確認的事實、哪些仍是詮釋或推測。
  • 指出盲目相信 AI 與全盤否定 AI 看似相反，卻都可能跳過親自提問、檢驗與反覆查證的關鍵步驟。
  • 結合作者早年接觸網際網路與初次使用聊天式 AI 的回憶，帶出 AI 不只是工具升級，也可能改變人與智慧互動的方式。

摘要

一段令作者驚喜，也引起警覺的 AI 對話

作者長期使用 AI。有一次工作時，中島美雪的〈竹之歌〉吸引了他的注意；他停下工作聽完整首歌，接著問 AI，這首歌為何如此有人味。作者表示自己其實聽不懂歌詞，AI 卻給出一段深刻而動人的回答，甚至寫道：「那根竹子，也在你的心裡生長。」這番話令他感到震撼，同時也讓他開始警覺：與 AI 有了這樣親密的對話後，人還會願意把相同的想法分享給身邊真實的人嗎？

動人文字不等於經過驗證的分析

作者逐句回看 AI 的回答。AI 描寫旋律不斷下沉、又努力上揚，並形容歌聲像是有人強忍淚水、微微顫抖；這些描述彷彿出自真正聽過歌曲的分析，但作者指出，文字聽起來像分析，不代表 AI 確實從音訊本身進行了分析。它究竟依據網路評論、歌曲風格，還是自行生成的文學式推測，作者並未查證。

AI 也把竹子的意象連結到東亞人的集體潛意識，甚至形容這種共鳴「刻在骨子裡」。作者認為這種說法感染力很強，卻仍是修辭，而非已被嚴格證明的因果結論。至於「聽不懂歌詞，理性翻譯的防線便降低，情緒更容易直接受到觸動」的說法，雖然優雅且合乎邏輯，作者也提醒，這可能只是模型為回應問題組織出的解釋，不一定是普遍適用的心理定律。回答寫得溫暖、漂亮，並不能保證其中的事實可信。

保留感動，也保留判斷

作者拆解後發現，這段回答中能客觀驗證的內容很少，多數是詮釋、推測與文學修辭。但這不代表對話毫無價值：AI 提供了作者原本缺乏的詞彙，讓他得以描述直覺，也從新的角度重新理解當時的感動。感動並沒有因此消失，理性辨別也仍然可以存在。

作者建議，下一次遇到 AI 看似深刻、富有哲理的長篇回答，可以挑出最打動自己的那一句，追問它的依據；在把內容轉述給朋友之前，也先分辨哪些部分是已確認的事實，哪些部分需要再查證。如此一來，人便能在欣賞文字的同時，練習判斷其可信程度。

超越盲信與全盤否定

作者指出，面對 AI 常見兩種極端反應：一種人把 AI 當成無所不知的存在，將流暢的描述直接當作事實，忽略它可能產生幻覺、編造內容；另一種人則認定 AI 只會空談，因而徹底否定它的價值。兩者表面上立場相反，實際上卻犯了相同的錯誤：都沒有親自拿真實問題去測試、質疑並反覆驗證。

作者認為，開放與批判並非在盲信和懷疑之間取一個溫吞的折衷，而是可以同時具備的能力。人既可以接納 AI 帶來的啟發，也可以持續檢查它的依據，不必在「奉為神明」與「視若垃圾」之間二選一。

作者記憶中的兩次「打開新世界」

為解釋自己為何如此重視 AI，作者回想約三十年前的 1990 年代。當時他親自讓公司網路連上網際網路，撥接數據機發出的尖銳雜音，令他感到興奮，因為那代表另一端即將接通，一個新世界正向他展開。幾年前，作者初讀 GPT-3 撰寫的文章時並未特別震撼；直到約四年前，他真正打開聊天視窗，與 GPT-3.5 一問一答，才彷彿再次聽見當年撥接上網的聲音。

在作者看來，早年的網路把世界各地的資訊與人帶到眼前；如今螢幕另一端則是一種全新的智慧，隨時能傾聽私密、瑣碎、未必有實際用途的問題，並展開深入對話。因此，他認為 AI 帶來的變化可能比工業革命、資訊科技或行動網路更深遠，並非單純的工具升級，而是人類歷史的一個分水嶺。影片最後，作者設想若朋友詢問 AI 究竟是什麼，他不會先談模型架構或參數，而會講述這段親身經歷；提供的字幕在此處中斷。

================================================

# 开场：话都说给 AI 了

When a very private thought pops into your mind, is your first reaction to talk to someone around you, or to open a chat window and talk to AI? At the end of this month, ChatGPT turns four years old. It is always on standby and always considerate, but this is precisely the most dangerous side of AI. I have been using AI seriously for almost four years now. Once, while I was working, I had some music playing in the background. Only a few lines into a song, the melody and the vocals instantly pulled my.

# 一首听不懂的歌

attention away from my work. I stopped what I was doing to listen to the whole song, and then I casually asked AI, "Why does Miyuki Nakajima's ' Song of Bamboo' possess such a human-like power?" It was so strange; I told it I couldn't understand the lyrics at all. Its answer was incredibly exciting, so philosophical and deeply moving. But later, the very same reason that excited me also made me feel vigilant. After we have had such deep conversations with AI, will we still share these same things with the real people around us? constantly sinks and struggles to rise. And that there is a trembling in the singer's voice of holding back tears. : it starts with a compliment about my keen sensitivity and ends by landing on the idea that "that bamboo also grows in your heart." The whole passage reads very warmly and comfortably; it feels very satisfying, and I know this way of expression is highly empathetic. Look, when I peel back this entire answer layer by layer and lay it on the table, you will notice an interesting phenomenon: there are actually very few. objective, strictly verifiable facts in the entire response; most of it is interpretation, speculation, and literary rhetoric. So, after breaking it down like this, does it mean this conversation was meaningless, or even that the AI is just talking nonsense? Not at all; it still provided me with great inspiration. which parts actually need you to double-check? When you can naturally make this distinction yourself, you have already started to move beyond binary thinking. descriptions like "the melody sinks and rises" or "a sense of nothingness etched in the bones," they’ll immediately think the AI is omniscient and might even forward those diagnostic words as facts . around me still haven't touched AI today , not necessarily because they are closed-minded, but more often simply because it's unfamiliar, because they haven't encountered an indispensable scenario in their daily work, or because they tried an early model a year or two ago and were discouraged by the poor experience. stops at nitpicking, it easily turns into cynicism; if openness stops at marveling at the magic of new technology , it easily turns into cheap fanaticism . Broad domain knowledge, the curiosity to solve the same problem in multiple ways, and a focus on core. competencies—these are the true origins of being able to "find a way." We can also check if the underlying project files can be modified directly. Then, force yourself to break out of. your current plan and find a different entry point. The standard for checking is simple: see if the new path you've devised actually changes the point of intervention, or if it just rephrases the original approach . Select the solution that is easiest to verify and let AI help you test it; if it fails, analyze what this failure has successfully ruled out. Then, we take this new insight and try the next path. the MAPS framework I summarized—Mindset , Architecture, Prompt, and System—I always place' M 'for Mindset at the very beginning. The mastery of any new technology and the improvement of human capability are essentially inseparable from shifts in your mindset. You see, facing a problem , "having a way to think" and "losing your way" are actually two completely different types of obstacles. "Having a way to think" relies on our daily accumulation of knowledge, curiosity,. and task decomposition; "willing to find a way" relies on not expecting to know which path is 100%successful before starting, being willing to face repeated failures, and remaining calm enough to try the next one. Whenever I encounter a difficult problem, many potential solutions often pop into my mind. I test them one by one according to priority. For a long time, I felt that this problem-solving intuition was something that could only be experienced , not taught. So, one of the most important reasons for creating the Maps framework and writing this book is to try to break. that limitation, articulate this multi-path problem-solving ability, and teach it to others. hold exactly the same view. Both scenarios imply the AI has made a mistake. But the danger I'm describing doesn't require the AI to err at all. On the contrary, when its answers are incredibly accurate, profound, and helpful, the very need you sought to express may already be fully satisfied. right there. The higher the quality of the conversation, the greater that sense of satisfaction becomes, and the less urgent the need feels to repeat those same words to a living person. 一段令作者驚喜，也引起警覺的 AI 對話

作者長期使用 AI。有一次工作時，中島美雪的〈竹之歌〉吸引了他的注意；他停下工作聽完整首歌，接著問 AI，這首歌為何如此有人味。作者表示自己其實聽不懂歌詞，AI 卻給出一段深刻而動人的回答，甚至寫道：「那根竹子，也在你的心裡生長。」這番話令他感到震撼，同時也讓他開始警覺：與 AI 有了這樣親密的對話後，人還會願意把相同的想法分享給身邊真實的人嗎？

動人文字不等於經過驗證的分析

作者逐句回看 AI 的回答。AI 描寫旋律不斷下沉、又努力上揚，並形容歌聲像是有人強忍淚水、微微顫抖；這些描述彷彿出自真正聽過歌曲的分析，但作者指出，文字聽起來像分析，不代表 AI 確實從音訊本身進行了分析。它究竟依據網路評論、歌曲風格，還是自行生成的文學式推測，作者並未查證。

AI 也把竹子的意象連結到東亞人的集體潛意識，甚至形容這種共鳴「刻在骨子裡」。作者認為這種說法感染力很強，卻仍是修辭，而非已被嚴格證明的因果結論。至於「聽不懂歌詞，理性翻譯的防線便降低，情緒更容易直接受到觸動」的說法，雖然優雅且合乎邏輯，作者也提醒，這可能只是模型為回應問題組織出的解釋，不一定是普遍適用的心理定律。回答寫得溫暖、漂亮，並不能保證其中的事實可信。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 透過作者與 AI 討論中島美雪歌曲的親身經驗，呈現 AI 如何用文字引發共鳴，也提醒讀者不要把動人的表達誤認為可靠的事實。
  • 提供實用的查證方法：遇到看似深刻的回答，可以追問依據，並分辨哪些是已確認的事實、哪些仍是詮釋或推測。
  • 指出盲目相信 AI 與全盤否定 AI 看似相反，卻都可能跳過親自提問、檢驗與反覆查證的關鍵步驟。
  • 結合作者早年接觸網際網路與初次使用聊天式 AI 的回憶，帶出 AI 不只是工具升級，也可能改變人與智慧互動的方式。

摘要

一段令作者驚喜，也引起警覺的 AI 對話

作者長期使用 AI。有一次工作時，中島美雪的〈竹之歌〉吸引了他的注意；他停下工作聽完整首歌，接著問 AI，這首歌為何如此有人味。作者表示自己其實聽不懂歌詞，AI 卻給出一段深刻而動人的回答，甚至寫道：「那根竹子，也在你的心裡生長。」這番話令他感到震撼，同時也讓他開始警覺：與 AI 有了這樣親密的對話後，人還會願意把相同的想法分享給身邊真實的人嗎？

動人文字不等於經過驗證的分析

作者逐句回看 AI 的回答。AI 描寫旋律不斷下沉、又努力上揚，並形容歌聲像是有人強忍淚水、微微顫抖；這些描述彷彿出自真正聽過歌曲的分析，但作者指出，文字聽起來像分析，不代表 AI 確實從音訊本身進行了分析。它究竟依據網路評論、歌曲風格，還是自行生成的文學式推測，作者並未查證。

AI 也把竹子的意象連結到東亞人的集體潛意識，甚至形容這種共鳴「刻在骨子裡」。作者認為這種說法感染力很強，卻仍是修辭，而非已被嚴格證明的因果結論。至於「聽不懂歌詞，理性翻譯的防線便降低，情緒更容易直接受到觸動」的說法，雖然優雅且合乎邏輯，作者也提醒，這可能只是模型為回應問題組織出的解釋，不一定是普遍適用的心理定律。回答寫得溫暖、漂亮，並不能保證其中的事實可信。

保留感動，也保留判斷

作者拆解後發現，這段回答中能客觀驗證的內容很少，多數是詮釋、推測與文學修辭。但這不代表對話毫無價值：AI 提供了作者原本缺乏的詞彙，讓他得以描述直覺，也從新的角度重新理解當時的感動。感動並沒有因此消失，理性辨別也仍然可以存在。

作者建議，下一次遇到 AI 看似深刻、富有哲理的長篇回答，可以挑出最打動自己的那一句，追問它的依據；在把內容轉述給朋友之前，也先分辨哪些部分是已確認的事實，哪些部分需要再查證。如此一來，人便能在欣賞文字的同時，練習判斷其可信程度。

超越盲信與全盤否定

作者指出，面對 AI 常見兩種極端反應：一種人把 AI 當成無所不知的存在，將流暢的描述直接當作事實，忽略它可能產生幻覺、編造內容；另一種人則認定 AI 只會空談，因而徹底否定它的價值。兩者表面上立場相反，實際上卻犯了相同的錯誤：都沒有親自拿真實問題去測試、質疑並反覆驗證。

作者認為，開放與批判並非在盲信和懷疑之間取一個溫吞的折衷，而是可以同時具備的能力。人既可以接納 AI 帶來的啟發，也可以持續檢查它的依據，不必在「奉為神明」與「視若垃圾」之間二選一。

作者記憶中的兩次「打開新世界」

為解釋自己為何如此重視 AI，作者回想約三十年前的 1990 年代。當時他親自讓公司網路連上網際網路，撥接數據機發出的尖銳雜音，令他感到興奮，因為那代表另一端即將接通，一個新世界正向他展開。幾年前，作者初讀 GPT-3 撰寫的文章時並未特別震撼；直到約四年前，他真正打開聊天視窗，與 GPT-3.5 一問一答，才彷彿再次聽見當年撥接上網的聲音。

在作者看來，早年的網路把世界各地的資訊與人帶到眼前；如今螢幕另一端則是一種全新的智慧，隨時能傾聽私密、瑣碎、未必有實際用途的問題，並展開深入對話。因此，他認為 AI 帶來的變化可能比工業革命、資訊科技或行動網路更深遠，並非單純的工具升級，而是人類歷史的一個分水嶺。影片最後，作者設想若朋友詢問 AI 究竟是什麼，他不會先談模型架構或參數，而會講述這段親身經歷；提供的字幕在此處中斷。

When a very private thought pops into your mind, is your first reaction to talk to someone around you, or to open a chat window and talk to AI? At the end of this month, ChatGPT turns four years old. attention away from my work. I stopped what I was doing to listen to the whole song, and then I casually asked AI, "Why does Miyuki Nakajima's ' Song of Bamboo' possess such a human-like power?" It was so strange; I told it I couldn't understand the lyrics at all. Its answer was incredibly exciting, so philosophical and deeply moving. But later, the very same reason that excited me also made me feel vigilant. After we have had such deep conversations with AI, will we still share these same things with the real people around us? Hey, hello, and welcome back. What is displayed on the screen is its complete response from that time. It provided a very long reply, so I will only read a few parts that truly moved me. # 把 AI 的回答一句句拆开

constantly sinks and struggles to rise. And that there is a trembling in the singer's voice of holding back tears. These words are written so realistically , just as if it had just finished listening to the whole song, but we must clarify one thing: a text that sounds like it has heard the song does not mean it actually performed a real analysis of the audio at the base level. What exactly was it basing its description on? Is this based on online reviews of the song, or is it a literary conjecture generated based on the style. of the lyrics and melody? I didn't verify it, and I don't need to guess for the AI. Let's look at the second point, which claims that the imagery of bamboo is a collective unconscious for East Asians, even suggesting this resonance is "etched in our bones." This sentence reads with great emotional intensity and can really strike a chord with native speakers, but...If you calm down and think about it, "etched in our bones" is a highly infectious literary rhetorical device; it is not a strictly proven causal conclusion. It sounds profound, but rhetorical praise remains just that. —rhetoric. For the third point, it offers a very deep explanation, saying that because we don't understand the lyrics, the rational translation layer is shut down, lowering our defenses and making it easier for emotions to be struck directly. But whether it is a universally valid psychological rule or just a rationalization the model organized to respond to my question, I also didn't verify it. Finally, look at its opening and closing.

: it starts with a compliment about my keen sensitivity and ends by landing on the idea that "that bamboo also grows in your heart." The whole passage reads very warmly and comfortably; it feels very satisfying, and I know this way of expression is highly empathetic. But just because a passage reads beautifully does not mean it provides a guarantee for the credibility of its facts. Look, when I peel back this entire answer layer by layer and lay it on the table, you will notice an interesting phenomenon: there are actually very few. objective, strictly verifiable facts in the entire response; most of it is interpretation, speculation, and literary rhetoric. So, after breaking it down like this, does it mean this conversation was meaningless, or even that the AI is just talking nonsense? Not at all; it still provided me with great inspiration. It gave me vocabulary I didn't have before to describe my intuition, and allowed me to examine that sense of shock from a new perspective; that moving feeling didn't disappear, while rational discernment also remained. This ability to discern can actually be trained at any time, and it is not mysterious at all. The next time you use AI, no matter what you ask it to analyze, when it spits out a long, seemingly profound and philosophical answer, try picking out that one sentence that struck a chord in your heart and ask it: what is the basis for that statement? which parts actually need you to double-check? When you can naturally make this distinction yourself, you have already started to move beyond binary thinking. So, your mindset must ultimately be in your hands, becoming the ladder-climbing ability to find a way and being willing to try when you face a specific, concrete problem. I'll share a real case I encountered while making a video; I wanted to add a typing effect to the subtitles. For video editing software, I used Jianying. At the time, the system's. recognized animation duration was only 0.5 seconds, which caused a major issue . For long sentences, the animation flashes by, making the effect barely noticeable. To simulate a real subtitle-following effect, you just need to extend the animation duration to match the subtitle length. But if you manually drag every subtitle in the software, it's obviously super inefficient. So, naturally, I wondered if I could get AI to write some code to handle this. I fed the Jianying project file to Claude and asked it to write a script to. set the animation duration to match the subtitle duration. Claude wrote the code quickly, and then I ran the script. The code ran without any errors, but when I reopened Jianying, I found the animation durations on the timeline hadn't changed at all—it didn't work. I kept having it search for the fix, but it kept getting it wrong every time. The lack of errors is a clue, but it doesn't explain where the problem lies. Eventually, I had to examine the Jianying project file structure myself, and after looking, I realized it had. misinterpreted the relationship between the animations and the subtitles. I explained this underlying logic to Claude, and it immediately produced the corrected code. I ran the code again, reopened the project file, and all the animation durations were perfectly matched to the subtitle lengths; the problem was solved. However, I want you to think carefully: how did I come up with this path? As I mentioned in my video at the time, first, I had a general understanding of Jianying's style, knowing it had many preset effects.

So I guessed it might be capable of better subtitle effects. More importantly, I noticed the Jianying project file format was text-based, meaning we could directly modify it. These solutions don't come from thin air . My usual understanding of the tools ' underlying features came into play at that moment, and in that video, I mentioned three directions for training this ability. Broad domain knowledge, the curiosity to solve the same problem in multiple ways, and a focus on core. competencies—these are the true origins of being able to "find a way." The emergence of AI has wiped out the skill of proficiently coding in a specific language in a very short time; you only need to clarify your requirements and logic, and it can build the code for you. But once this layer is leveled, what truly creates a gap is whether you can think of alternative paths when facing specific problems, and your ability to patiently troubleshoot when AI fails. For the same goal, we can actually intervene at different points: we can drag tracks in the editing software's main interface, or look for global batch settings within the software's features . We can also check if the underlying project files can be modified directly. The next time you get stuck on a real-world problem, try using it as an exercise: first, clearly identify the solution you are currently using. Where exactly are you taking action? Then, force yourself to break out of. your current plan and find a different entry point. The standard for checking is simple: see if the new path you've devised actually changes the point of intervention, or if it just rephrases the original approach . Select the solution that is easiest to verify and let AI help you test it; if it fails, analyze what this failure has successfully ruled out. Then, we take this new insight and try the next path. At this point, you can understand why in.

# 为什么 M 排在最前面

the MAPS framework I summarized—Mindset , Architecture, Prompt, and System—I always place' M 'for Mindset at the very beginning. The mastery of any new technology and the improvement of human capability are essentially inseparable from shifts in your mindset. You see, facing a problem , "having a way to think" and "losing your way" are actually two completely different types of obstacles. "Having a way to think" relies on our daily accumulation of knowledge, curiosity,. and task decomposition; "willing to find a way" relies on not expecting to know which path is 100%successful before starting, being willing to face repeated failures, and remaining calm enough to try the next one. Whenever I encounter a difficult problem, many potential solutions often pop into my mind. I test them one by one according to priority. Only after all these paths have been tried and the problem remains unsolved do I conclude that the current version of me cannot solve it. Note that I included the qualifier "the. current version of me." In the vast majority of cases, there is no need to try all the options; the problem is solved at some intermediate step. This is entirely a matter of Mindset. Of course, I don’t mean that there is any mechanical separation or strict division of labor between these four letters. The curiosity and desire for exploration you have cultivated normally run through the process of coming up with various paths . However, if you are afraid of failure and only want a guaranteed, risk-free standard answer, then no matter how. advanced the AI you have, if the first attempt is unsatisfactory, the entire problem-solving process may come to a complete end. Therefore, M must come first. This intuition of diverging into multiple paths when encountering a problem and verifying them one by one is the result of my years of engineering training. For a long time, I felt that this problem-solving intuition was something that could only be experienced , not taught. So, one of the most important reasons for creating the Maps framework and writing this book is to try to break. that limitation, articulate this multi-path problem-solving ability, and teach it to others. How to teach? You have actually seen that if I only post the final code that works, aside from letting people exclaim, "AI is amazing, " or "The author is great," everyone learns nothing. Why did I think of this path? Only by showing the inspection methods when the code fails, the sticking points when things aren't working, and the process of changing direction can everyone clearly see how the problem is. solved step by step. Putting the process of failure and adjustment on the table. That in itself is a teaching method, but I also want to talk about another side of this openness . This side is not about productivity, but about our real lives. I once posted a tweet; this was my view at the time: the higher the quality of deep dialogue with an AI, the lower the sense of urgency to say the same things to a living person. This is the only structural threat AI poses to our lives ; it is greater than hallucinations or goal drift. Looking at it today, I still.

hold exactly the same view. Those working in AI often discuss the technical risks of models, such as hallucinations—where the AI confidently invents facts that don't exist—or goal drift, where the AI veers away from its original objective while performing a task. Both scenarios imply the AI has made a mistake. But the danger I'm describing doesn't require the AI to err at all. On the contrary, when its answers are incredibly accurate, profound, and helpful, the very need you sought to express may already be fully satisfied. right there. The higher the quality of the conversation, the greater that sense of satisfaction becomes, and the less urgent the need feels to repeat those same words to a living person. This is why I call it a structural risk. Remember the reflection I shared at the beginning after listening to that Miyuki Nakajima song? That was the AI's response. It’s hard to imagine anyone sitting next to you being able to engage in such a profound conversation if you just asked them off the cuff. Looking back today, the reason I felt so incredibly excited at the time is exactly what corresponds to the deep sense of caution I feel now. Of course, we must distinguish between things; refraining from constantly venting to those around us or dumping chaotic emotions onto our loved ones is often a form of maturity itself. If a deep conversation helps you sort out your thoughts and enables you to face reality more clearly, then that is certainly a good thing. But I am always focused on the direction of that gravity: after the conversation ends, are you better equipped to return to reality and communicate with people, or have you unknowingly begun reserving. fewer and fewer meaningful experiences for the real people around you? Conversations between humans have never been solely about efficiently explaining a matter. They are filled with pauses, hesitations, and clashes of viewpoints. 摘要

模型選擇的迷思與實測背景

作者指出，許多人在面對 Anthropic 的 Claude 系列模型及思考預算切換開關時，往往會依照直覺挑選，但這些選擇背後卻暗藏成本翻倍或性能不符預期的陷阱。例如使用輕量級模型進行多輪編程時可能觸發高倍費率，或開啟最高智慧等級卻多付了將近兩成費用且未帶來明顯效益。為了釐清真相，作者針對多種配置與模式展開了相同條件下的橫向評測，從生成品質、耗費時間與API 成本進行深度剖析。

第一輪測試：3D 越野車越障模擬

第一項挑戰要求模型在完全斷網的環境下，撰寫出能夠翻越 18 公分減速帶的3D 越野車動力模擬。雖然所有配置皆成功運行，但在細節呈現上差距甚大。高階配置成功還原了雨後地面積水倒影、乾淨車窗以及與實車相同的並列彈簧避震結構；官方預設模式則以最快速度與適中成本取得極佳平衡。相對地，低階模型不僅材質簡陋，甚至出現了煞車卡鉗隨輪胎轉動的荒謬機械錯誤。

第二輪測試：精細機械蝴蝶與展開視圖

第二項測試聚焦於多層微型零件聯動，要求模型打造出兼具金屬鏤空、彩繪玻璃與胸腔齒輪聯動的互動式 3D 機械蝴蝶，並支援一鍵爆炸圖拆解。在此測試中，中低階模型紛紛暴露出過曝、透明度欠佳或結構如玩具般的缺陷。兩款頂級配置在細節與節奏感上難分伯仲，但作者特別指出，開啟最高思考預算的模式耗時與費用足足翻倍，肉眼可見的成果卻無實質差距。

第三輪測試：長文本空間組裝導引

第三輪任務考驗長文本理解與空間幾何組裝，模型需依據五頁英文家具手冊，將 32 個板材零件按孔位和順序轉化為互動組裝流程。這項測試徹底拉開了高低階之間的差距：低階模型組裝邏輯完全崩潰、桌面漂浮空中；中階模型能流暢運行卻遺漏了凹槽等細部特徵；唯有頂規配置能精準定位零件輪廓並嵌入手冊圖解，展現出處理複雜空間任務的強大實力。

only slightly more expensive than o1- preview. However, the trade-off is that it actually stumbled on visual judgment tasks, like reading clock hands. enough. Pushing to the X tier costs nearly 20%more, yet it didn’t win a single one of the four tasks. document Q&A, or lightweight development , choose SIT 5.5 H; it gets a perfect score on image tasks. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 避開費用陷阱：深入揭露 Claude 各模型與思考預算設定中「花費更高卻未必更好」的直覺誤區。
  • 多維度極限實測：透過無網路 3D 物理動態、精密機械連動與長文本空間組裝三大嚴苛任務，全方位檢驗真實代碼能力。
  • 性價比指南：提供詳細的時間、API 成本與生成細節對比，協助開發者依據實際場景選出最具成本效益的模型配置。

摘要

模型選擇的迷思與實測背景

作者指出，許多人在面對 Anthropic 的 Claude 系列模型及思考預算切換開關時，往往會依照直覺挑選，但這些選擇背後卻暗藏成本翻倍或性能不符預期的陷阱。例如使用輕量級模型進行多輪編程時可能觸發高倍費率，或開啟最高智慧等級卻多付了將近兩成費用且未帶來明顯效益。為了釐清真相，作者針對多種配置與模式展開了相同條件下的橫向評測，從生成品質、耗費時間與API 成本進行深度剖析。

第一輪測試：3D 越野車越障模擬

第一項挑戰要求模型在完全斷網的環境下，撰寫出能夠翻越 18 公分減速帶的3D 越野車動力模擬。雖然所有配置皆成功運行，但在細節呈現上差距甚大。高階配置成功還原了雨後地面積水倒影、乾淨車窗以及與實車相同的並列彈簧避震結構；官方預設模式則以最快速度與適中成本取得極佳平衡。相對地，低階模型不僅材質簡陋，甚至出現了煞車卡鉗隨輪胎轉動的荒謬機械錯誤。

第二輪測試：精細機械蝴蝶與展開視圖

第二項測試聚焦於多層微型零件聯動，要求模型打造出兼具金屬鏤空、彩繪玻璃與胸腔齒輪聯動的互動式 3D 機械蝴蝶，並支援一鍵爆炸圖拆解。在此測試中，中低階模型紛紛暴露出過曝、透明度欠佳或結構如玩具般的缺陷。兩款頂級配置在細節與節奏感上難分伯仲，但作者特別指出，開啟最高思考預算的模式耗時與費用足足翻倍，肉眼可見的成果卻無實質差距。

第三輪測試：長文本空間組裝導引

第三輪任務考驗長文本理解與空間幾何組裝，模型需依據五頁英文家具手冊，將 32 個板材零件按孔位和順序轉化為互動組裝流程。這項測試徹底拉開了高低階之間的差距：低階模型組裝邏輯完全崩潰、桌面漂浮空中；中階模型能流暢運行卻遺漏了凹槽等細部特徵；唯有頂規配置能精準定位零件輪廓並嵌入手冊圖解，展現出處理複雜空間任務的強大實力。

Intelligence" level, you'll pay nearly 20%more across four tests, yet it didn't outperform the standard Opus at all. requires running independently without a network, so I completely cut off the browser's external connection; tests showed all six modes had zero errors and ran successfully. structure and three-dimensional breakdown, creating a two-layer hollow metal wing frame with blue gradient stained glass and gears sandwiched in between, and a clear metal color separation inside the open chest.
